title: A Code-Agnostic Graph Neural Network Decoder from the Detection Error Model
abstract: We present POLYMECHANON, a graph neural network (GNN) decoder for quantum error correction whose only input is the detection error model (DEM) of a quantum code under a given noise model. We represent the DEM as a tripartite graph of detectors, error mechanisms and logical observables, where every input feature is computed by using the quantum code as data rather than design choice. In this way, the same architecture decodes in principle any stabiliser code, under any noise model that can be expressed as a detection error model, once trained on the DEM. We test this approach along four directions. Firstly, on the rotated surface code the decoder outperforms correlated MWPM under both phenomenological and circuit-level noise, with up to $25\%$ fewer logical failures. Secondly, on a family of high-rate qLDPC codes it matches BP+OSD on the smaller codes and surpasses it on the larger ones, with up to $16\%$ fewer logical failures on $[\![130,4,6]\!]$. Thirdly, its decoding time does not depend on the physical error rate, whereas that of BP+OSD grows with it: on $[\![130,4,6]\!]$ its effective cost per shot is of the order of a few ms on a single GPU against a few tens of milliseconds for BP+OSD on a single CPU core, and its fixed computational graph makes it a candidate for real-time decoding on neutral-atom processors. Finally, a single model trained across codes of different families outperforms uncorrelated MWPM on the graph-like codes seen during training and stays within $10\%$ of BP+OSD on the others, while it tends to fail to generalize to unseen codes, particularly larger ones. Its probabilistic output enables confidence-based post-selection, lowering the logical error rate by more than an order of magnitude on the surface code while keeping more than $90\%$ of the shots. Since only the DEM changes, new codes and noise models can be decoded without redesigning the decoder.
summary: This paper introduces POLYMECHANON, a Graph Neural Network decoder for quantum error correction that takes only the Detection Error Model (DEM) as input. It demonstrates that this single architecture can decode various stabilizer codes under different noise models, significantly outperforming existing methods in terms of error suppression and computational speed. This advances the field toward universal, hardware-independent quantum computation protocols.
main_problem: To develop a quantum error correction (QEC) decoder that is code-agnostic, meaning it can decode any stabilizer code under any noise model expressible as a Detection Error Model (DEM) without requiring redesign.
main_result: The proposed GNN decoder, POLYMECHANON, outperforms existing decoders on both surface and qLDPC codes, showing superior scaling and computational efficiency, and enabling confidence-based post-selection.
method: The authors use a Graph Neural Network (GNN) decoder whose input is the tripartite graph representation of the Detection Error Model (DEM) of the quantum code and noise structure.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum error correction using stabilizer codes, tested on the rotated surface code and high-rate qLDPC codes. The decoder operates on the DEM, which models detectors, error mechanisms, and logical observables.
key_observables: Logical Error Rate (LER), decoding time/cost, and the fraction of accepted shots after post-selection.
important_parameters: Physical error rate ($p$), code distance ($d$), and the confidence threshold ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the DEM alone contains sufficient information to characterize the decoding problem, allowing a single architecture to generalize across different codes and noise models.
figures_summary: Figures compare LER vs. physical error rate for different decoders (GNN vs. MWPM vs. BP+OSD) on surface and qLDPC codes, and show the effect of confidence-based post-selection on LER and shot acceptance.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the code-agnostic GNN decoder based on the DEM, validates its performance against state-of-the-art decoders on multiple code families and noise models, and details the benefits of probabilistic output for post-selection.
why_interesting: The focus on a code-agnostic decoder whose input is purely structural (the DEM) is highly relevant for building universal, hardware-agnostic quantum computation protocols.

Logical error rate of the GNN decoder (solid) against the classical decoder (dashed) as a function of the physical error rate p, on identical shots and with r=d syndrome rounds. The baseline is correlated minimum-weight perfect matching on the two surface-code panels and BP+OSD on the qLDPC panel.
FIG. 2. The two code families studied in this work.

FIG. 3. Representation of an extended Tanner graph. From left to right, the nodes are the detectors (D), the error mech- anisms (EM), and the logical observable (L) of the detection error model of a surface code. Edges encode which detectors are triggered by each error mechanism and which mechanisms flip the logical observable. An even number of triggers has no effect in the noise regimes that we operate with.

FIG. 4. Overview of the POLYMECHANON forward pass. The nine-dimensional node features are embedded via subtype- specific linear maps and non-linear activating functions. Over T iterations, representations are refined by NMP residual message- passing layers and updated by a GRU cell (Eq. 6). After, a FiLM conditioning is applied. The final output head maps the L-node representation to a logical error prediction.
